To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Treg frequency is higher in patients with a discordant response to antiretrovrial therapy than in subjects with a concordant response, and that the Treg counts are higher in HIV-infected patients who have not achieved a CD4+ T-cell count of 350 cells per µl after more than two year of treatment.

in the course of antiretrovial therapy, HIV-infected patients who have a discordant response to treatment develop an increase in the frequency of regulatory T cells in their blood, while the CD4+ T lymphocytes counts remain low.
the frequency of regulatory T lymphocyte counts in patients with HIV infection and a discordant response to antiretrovial therapy is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of HIV‑infec-tion progression in patients with a low CD4+ lymphocyte count and a discordant immune system restoration.
the role of Treg in the pathogenesis of HIV infection.
the study of the immune status of HIV-infected subjects and the development of new approaches to the treatment of this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Treg counts are not a prognostic marker of the immune system response in HIV‑infected patients.
Treg deficiency is associated with an impaired response to antiretrovial therapy.
the Treg deficiency in HIV-infected patients is associated with an increase in the frequency of Treg cells in their peripheral blood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increase in Treg frequency in HIV-infected individuals with discordant response is a result of the Treg proliferation in response to the immune system activation.
the immune system of HIV-infected patients is characterized by a low Treg content and an increased Treg frequency in the blood.
the increase in regulatory T cell frequency in the blood of patients with low CD4+ counts is a marker of poor response to the antiretrovital therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD4+ Treg counts should be considered in the clinical assessment of patients with HIV‑1 infection.
the Treg count is an important marker of immune system restoration in HIV‑infected patients.
a low CD4+ count and the accumulation of regulatory T cells are associated with a discordant immune response in HIV-infected patients.
